ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the New Zealand Sanctions Register (MFAT), UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, United States OFAC SDN List, UK HMT sanctions list, and Australian DFAT consolidated list; Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) screening required under AML/CFT Act 2009 sections 16–17 and FMA/DIA AML/CFT supervisory expectations, including enhanced due diligence (EDD) for foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates; ongoing transaction monitoring and sanctions screening on a real-time or risk-based periodic basis (at least every 24 hours for sanctions list updates) for all API platform payment flows, including Stripe and USDC cryptocurrency rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Register of Companies (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English or te reo Māori script; the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or reserved name; names may include numbers and common punctuation, but must be capable of being rendered in the Latin alphabet; where a non-English name is proposed, an English translation or transliteration must be provided and assessed for prohibited meaning and availability; names must not imply a connection with the Crown, the New Zealand Government, or any international body unless prior written consent is obtained.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant must first seek clarification from the Companies Office via the online inquiry function within 5 working days of the rejection notice; if a statutory basis for rejection is disputed, the applicant may file a formal administrative complaint to the Registrar of Companies under section 364 of the Companies Act 1993, attaching a legal memorandum and any consents from relevant ministry for sensitive words; the Registrar must respond within 20 working days; if the response is adverse, the applicant may lodge an appeal to the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972 (now Senior Courts Act 2016) for judicial review; alternate preferred name reservations can be re-submitted immediately without monetary penalty; each reservation order grants a 20-working-day exclusive reservation window, extendable once for a further 20 working days upon written request and payment of the extension fee before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for registered office and director service address purposes, provided the service provider is an approved New Zealand Company Office agent with a physical street address in New Zealand; however, for an AI/LLM API platform with target payment rails of Stripe and USDC, the practical merchant underwriting and VASP/PSP compliance expectations require a substance address, physical operational presence or at least demonstrable commercial substance (local director, locally banked operational account, and real contract management capability) to mitigate AML/CFT risk; a pure virtual office without any employee or operational nexus will likely trigger enhanced due diligence, payment processor holds, or termination.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium (estimated 35–45% probability within the first 18 months of operation) for a company that publicly markets AI/LLM API services and processes both fiat (Stripe) and cryptocurrency (USDC) payments, because the AML/CFT Act 2009 requires supervised entities (including trust and company service providers) to conduct ongoing due diligence and site visits where risk triggers exist; the Companies Office does not routinely conduct physical inspections, but Inland Revenue and the Financial Markets Authority or DIA may request proof of business premises and operational substance in response to payment processor queries, banking AML reviews, or mental health / child safety / gambling / securities regulatory complaints; unannounced inspection risk increases if the registered office is only a virtual mailbox and the company's stated data residency or privacy compliance claims are not verifiable.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), principally ss 3 (capacity and powers), 4 (incorporation), 5 (constitution), 6 (name requirements), 10 (contents of constitution), 12 (application for registration), 19 (certificate of incorporation), 22 (availability of names), 29 (correction of register), 44 (share capital), 110-112 (director appointments), and 189-194 (directors' duties); Income Tax Act 2007 ss YB 1-14 (tax residence rules for non-resident-exempt status); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 for corporate KYC obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), 15 Stout Street, Wellington, New Zealand; online filing via the New Zealand Companies Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (electronic statutory form lodged through the New Zealand Companies Register pursuant to s 12 of the Companies Act 1993), accompanied by the company constitution and consents to act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital exists under the Companies Act 1993; the company may be incorporated with nil issued capital, and shares may be allotted for consideration fixed by the board per ss 44-58. No escrow account, capital deposit, or proof-of-funds requirement applies to the Registrar. If capital is subscribed, the proceeds must be applied to lawful corporate purposes and recorded in the share register under s 88.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: This formal resolution is made on the date of incorporation at the registered office of the company, being a duly constituted meeting of the board of directors of [COMPANY NAME] Limited (company number ____________). It is resolved as follows: 1. SUBSCRIPTION OF SHARE CAPITAL: That the allotment of the initial share capital be, and it is, approved; the board authorises the issue of [1,000] ordinary shares at NZ$[0.01] each to the founding subscriber, with consideration recorded in the share register; no escrow or capital deposit is required under the Companies Act 1993. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: That the registered office of the company is fixed and recorded in New Zealand at [address], and the board appoints [name] as the person authorised to accept service of documents. 3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: That the following officers are appointed to hold office until the next annual general meeting or until earlier succession: (a) [Name], director; (b) [Name], company secretary, if required; and (c) [Name], chief financial officer and AML/CTF compliance officer. 4. BANKING AND SIGNING: That the board authorises the opening of corporate bank accounts, payment rails, and the execution of documents with the signature of any two directors, in accordance with the company's constitution. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Workplace Premises and Municipal Compliance Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local territorial authority (city/district council); Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ); WorkSafe New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the company leases an office or server-hosting space, verify that the building holds a current building warrant of fitness (BWOF) under the Building Act 2004, that the fire evacuation scheme is approved by FENZ, and that electrical infrastructure for IT equipment meets the Electricity (Safety) Regulations 2010. Lodge a workplace notification with WorkSafe if any hazardous substances or high-risk plant are present; for a pure software operation, no industrial operating permit is mandated. Secure any local municipal business licence required by each territorial authority's planning by-laws.
required_dossiers: Executed lease or registered office arrangement
Building warrant of fitness certificate and compliance schedule
Fire evacuation scheme approval from FENZ
Structural load assessment for server racks (if applicable)
Workplace health and safety policy under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the territorial authority identifies compliance deficiencies, remedy through a remedial works notice (ss 164-168 Building Act 2004) and re-inspection. For FENZ queries, revise and resubmit the fire evacuation scheme within the stated response period; appeal adverse council decisions to the Environment Court under the Resource Management Act 1991 if a resource consent is required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) – Workplace Health and Safety and Building Systems divisions; local territorial authority for premises compliance; no dedicated industrial licensing board applies to pure ISIC 6201 software and AI API operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no statutory operating or manufacturing permit is mandated for ISIC 6201 (computer programming and software publishing). The company operates under its Certificate of Incorporation, with optional municipal business licence and building warrant of fitness where physical premises are occupied.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, acting under the Resource Management Act 1991 and the Environmental Protection Authority Act 2011
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category 'Exempt / No EIA Required'. Pure software engineering, LLM inference, and API platform operations generate no land, water, or air discharges; a Full EIA Report or Assessment of Environmental Effects is not required. A resource consent would become mandatory only if the company later constructs or operates a physical data centre with significant energy and waste streams.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source effluent or VOC thresholds apply to zero-discharge software operations. For any IT hardware, the following standards apply: (a) wastewater – zero discharge from office and server premises, with trade waste consent per local council by-laws if cooling utilities are installed; (b) e-waste – compliance with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and the New Zealand e-waste voluntary product stewardship scheme, requiring recovery of >90% of electronic components; (c) standby power of computing equipment below 1 W where feasible under the Energy Efficiency (Energy Using Products) Regulations; (d) refrigerants in server cooling must be non-ozone-depleting with global warming potential < 2,500 per the Ozone Layer Protection Act 1996.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance in the form of an annual building warrant of fitness (BWOF) pursuant to ss 100-108 of the Building Act 2004, issued after inspection of fire exits, alarms, and suppression systems; approval of a fire evacuation scheme by Fire and Emergency New Zealand under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017; structural load inspection of floor slabs and racking areas per NZS 3604 / NZ Structures Standard; and a workplace occupational clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including a worker engagement assessment, first aid provisions, and an asbestos register where any pre-2000 building is occupied.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue / Te Tari Taake), Government of New Zealand; online compliance portal: myIR at https://www.ird.govt.nz; border customs validation performed by the New Zealand Customs Service at https://www.customs.govt.nz.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned International Company (IC) seeking New Zealand tax identity: (1) Determine tax residency - an IC incorporated outside New Zealand is non-resident for income tax purposes unless it has a fixed establishment in New Zealand; an IC incorporated in New Zealand is resident unless the application of a double tax agreement tie-breaker or a finding that central management and control is exercised offshore establishes otherwise. (2) Apply to the Inland Revenue Department for an IRD number by submitting Form IR596 (Application for an IRD Number by a Non-Resident Company), together with the certified certificate of incorporation, constitution, register of directors and shareholders, and identity documentation for all directors and holders of 25 percent or more of the shares. (3) If the IC will make taxable supplies in New Zealand in excess of the NZD 60,000 registration threshold, or elects voluntary registration, register for GST by filing Form GST 101A (Non-Resident GST Registration) through myIR, designating a New Zealand agent for service of notices if required by Inland Revenue. (4) If the IC engages New Zealand-resident personnel, register as an employer and obtain an employer IRD number for PAYE purposes. (5) Finalize the registration by linking the entity to myIR, securing the IRD confirmation letter and GST registration certificate; IRD generally issues the IRD number within 10 to 15 working days and the GST certificate within 7 working days of a complete application.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available statutory elections and designations under New Zealand tax law: (1) Look-through company (LTC) election under Subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, rendering the IC fiscally transparent with income and losses flowing through to shareholders; (2) Consolidated group election under Subpart IC of the Income Tax Act 2007 for groups of companies with 66 percent or more common New Zealand resident ownership; (3) Exemption from income tax for a non-resident foreign IC that has no fixed establishment in New Zealand and derives no New Zealand-source income, consistently with the Tax_Exempt_Zone classification; (4) Hybrid mismatch elections and special reporting under Subpart FH of the Income Tax Act 2007, including the elective branch equivalent rule under section FH 7 and the optional tiering of hybrid instruments; (5) Dividend exemption elections under section CW 9 for fully-taxed or specifically-exempt non-resident dividends; (6) A binding tax position ruling under section 149A of the Tax Administration Act 1994 confirming the IC exempt non-resident status and GST registration position, being the principal elective mechanism to render the Tax_Exempt_Zone classification administratively conclusive in New Zealand.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) - Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (New Zealand)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies made in or imported into New Zealand in any 12-month period; the threshold applies equally to resident suppliers, non-resident suppliers of remote services, and operators of electronic marketplaces supplying digital services to New Zealand resident consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand operates no mandatory electronic invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance regime. E-invoicing is voluntary under the international Peppol framework administered by the Peppol Authority New Zealand; there are no continuous transaction controls, no API-based fiscal stamping, and no requirement for digital clearance certificates. GST returns are self-assessed and filed through myIR on a one-month, two-month, or six-month basis, with GST due on the 28th day following each taxable period. The Inland Revenue Department and the New Zealand Customs Service share electronic trade data, and zero-rated or out-of-scope export transactions remain subject to document-based audit verification rather than pre-clearance approval.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 is available to an IC supplying generative AI and LLM inference API services where: (a) the services are supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time of performance under section 11(2); (b) the services qualify as remote services and are not physically performed in New Zealand under sections 11A and 11B; (c) the supply does not relate to land, goods, or services physically enjoyed in New Zealand; and (d) contemporaneous commercial evidence, being executed contracts, invoices, offshore tax identification or KYC records, IP-address and server-access logs, usage metering reports, and foreign currency remittance records, demonstrates the offshore chain. Physical goods exported from New Zealand, such as edge-computing appliances, are zero-rated under section 11(1) upon exportation, supported by a Customs export declaration, bill of lading or airwaybill, and inward remittance evidence. A non-resident IC supplying exclusively to non-resident customers is outside the New Zealand GST system entirely and is not required to register; registration is triggered only if it supplies remote services to New Zealand resident consumers exceeding the NZD 60,000 threshold. A GST refund of input tax is available to a registered person on zero-rated or exported supplies; refunds to non-resident registered persons are paid to the designated New Zealand bank account established at registration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic declaration via ExDOC/Tradepoint or approved New Zealand Customs Service export entry) for physical exports
Bill of Lading or Airwaybill evidencing physical departure of goods from New Zealand
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or the corresponding bank SWIFT MT103/MT950 credit advice evidencing receipt of export consideration from the offshore buyer
Commercial invoice and executed service agreement specifying the offshore recipient, the nature of the AI/LLM API services, and the zero-rated or out-of-scope GST treatment
Non-residence evidence of the recipient (foreign tax identification number, tax residence certificate, official company registry extract, or equivalent KYC documentation)

Technology delivery and utilization records (API access logs, server and IP-address jurisdiction records, usage metering and billing outputs) substantiating that the supply was performed and consumed outside New Zealand
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue audits export zero-rating claims with concentrated scrutiny on the genuineness of offshore provision and on traceable foreign exchange repatriation. Where a zero-rating claim is reversed, the IC is assessed for the full 15 percent GST on the disputed supplies, plus use-of-money interest at the prescribed quarterly rate and shortfall penalties under Part 9 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, being 20 percent for an unacceptable tax position, 40 percent for gross carelessness, and 100 percent for fraudulent intent. Wrongly refunded or reclaimed GST is recoverable by the Commissioner under section 26 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, with assessments generally limited to four years under section 108 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 but unlimited in cases of fraud. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day window, or reliance upon irreconcilable or missing customs documentation such as absent bills of lading, customs export declarations, or inward remittance certificates, automatically exposes input credits claimed on export-related expenditure to clawback, triggers penalty loading, and may constitute grounds for criminal prosecution carrying fines of up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and the Crimes Act 1961.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua (RBNZ), acting jointly with the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for derivative and financial-market licensing. New Zealand maintains no dedicated exchange-control administration; the openness of the New Zealand capital account is a statutory feature of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 and the unilateral commitment under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement, which obliges New Zealand to refrain from imposing restrictions on current international payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully convertible on both current and capital account. No exchange-control approval is required for the conversion of NZD into foreign currency, the crediting of foreign currency export revenues, the repatriation of share capital, or the distribution of profits. Profit remittance is achieved without material impediment; the only residual friction is the operation of the non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) regime under the Income Tax Act 2007 and the requirement under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act) that commercial banks verify the source and destination of outward payments. For a tax-exempt international company whose operations are limited to the cross-border supply of tokenised AI inference services, the convertibility profile is unrestricted, subject to standard AML/CFT documentary evidence. No capital gains tax is imposed on share dispositions by non-residents, and there is no branch remittance tax or dividend-control licence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory obligation to repatriate, surrender, or convert export proceeds. Any legal or natural person may retain 100% of hard-currency receipts in domiciled foreign-currency accounts, and may selectively convert into NZD at commercial rates. There is no prescribed timeline within which outward or inward trade settlements must be cleared. The only mandatory reporting arises in respect of balance-of-payments statistics (via reserve bank data collection and aggregated banking statistics) and tax compliance; the AI API platform must file annual income tax returns and charge goods and services tax (GST) at 0% for exported digital services, and should maintain transfer-pricing documentation for related-party platform usage fees.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of New Zealand (BNZ, a division of National Australia Bank Limited)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Regulatory viability: Medium-to-High, but with structural limitations. New Zealand licensed money remitters and non-bank financial institutions (operating under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and regulated under the AML/CFT Act 2009) may provide multi-currency transaction accounts to companies, including foreign-owned tax-exempt international companies, yet they do not hold a banking licence and therefore cannot offer deposit-taking facilities, overdraft commitments, or direct membership of the RBNZ's Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS). Offshore electronic-money institutions domiciled in the EU or UK do not automatically passport into New Zealand; an NZ Financial Service Provider (FSP) registration, NZ-based AML/CFT compliance officer, and FSPR membership are mandatory prerequisites. For USDC-heavy treasury flows, an NZ-registered Virtual Asset Service Provider (VASP) conversion layer is legally mandatory; direct crypto-custodial banking at Tier 1 banks is unavailable in New Zealand, though the platform may convert USDC to NZD via regulated digital-asset exchanges such as Independent Reserve NZ Limited or Easy Crypto Limited, followed by normal SWIFT or local NZD settlement into the Tier 1 bank accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The AML/CFT Act 2009 does not statutorily require an in-person meeting at a physical branch; identity verification can be performed electronically by the reporting entity using a certified digital identity service, biometric passport verification, or an independent Australian or New Zealand professional referrer. In practice, however, Tier 1 banks in New Zealand approach wholly non-resident, tax-exempt structures with heightened customer due diligence (CDD), and most institutions will require at least one director or ultimate beneficial owner to attend a live video-conference KYC interview before account opening. A minority of banks will further insist on an in-person visit at an Auckland or Christchurch corporate banking centre for first-time non-resident clients, especially when the corporate vehicle has no registered place of business in New Zealand. Prudent structuring: appoint one New Zealand-resident director or a domestic nominated signatory (in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 requirement that a resident director be appointed if the entity is registered under that Act), and include in the board resolution a treasury mandate authorising a New Zealand-based professional service provider to execute the account documents. For a Cook Islands-international-company style vehicle with corporate director, an executed certificate from the registered agent and apostilled documents will be required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wholly non-resident beneficial ownership combined with tax-exempt classification, creating perceived lack of economic nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation; constitutional documents; current certificate of good standing; full register of members and directors; ultimate beneficial ownership declaration; tax residency certificates of each shareholder; a formal opinion from New Zealand tax counsel confirming the tax-exempt character under the Income Tax Act 2007; the company's IRD number or a declaration of non-residence; audited or reviewed financial statements; and the group's operational service contract with a New Zealand-hosted data centre or cloud provider demonstrating at least demonstrable economic activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipt of USDC / cryptocurrency-derived funds into the corporate bank account, presenting money-laundering and sanctions-nexus concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written treasury policy prohibiting direct P2P transfers; evidence that all USDC is onboarded through an NZ-registered VASP subject to the AML/CFT Act 2009; blockchain-forensics transaction analysis (e.g., Chainalysis-style attestation) tracing the origin of acquired USDC; contracts with the custody provider and the exchange showing fiat-off-ramp methodology; monthly reconciliation of wallet addresses; sanctions screening reports for all material counterparties; and a legal memorandum on the travel-rule equivalent obligations under the AML/CFT (Requirements and Compliance) Regulations 2011 and the Financial Action Task Force's Recommendation 16.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket cross-border recurring invoices for AI/LLM API token usage, triggering pattern-scanning and unintended trade-reporting flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standard-form SaaS/API licence agreements; an extract of the billing platform's transaction ledger mapping token consumption to invoice lines; a schedule of whitelisted customers and counterparty due diligence files; identification of beneficial owners for corporate customers; a risk-based transaction monitoring override memorandum demonstrating the 'Low_Risk_Standard' classification; and evidence of an independent compliance audit engagement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital-escrow structure: a capital injection into a shell vehicle with no physical office or staff in New Zealand
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement; board resolution approving the capital call; source-of-funds documentation from the corporate parent (audited financial statements, dividend resolutions, or disposal contracts); an executed co-working or server-hosting lease in New Zealand; employment or consultancy agreements for locally resident technical and treasury personnel; a description of the AI GPU nodes resident in New Zealand cloud infrastructure; and a written confirmation that the Overseas Investment Act 2005 screening threshold is not crossed.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound institutional share capital subscriptions will be routed as telegraphic transfers using SWIFT MT103 for customer-originated payments and MT202 for interbank reimbursement, with the messaging narrative populated using ISO 20022 purpose code 'CAPT' (Payment of Securities-Related Fees) or 'COSP' (Capital Payments such as contributions to corporate capital). The remittance field should cite 'Share subscription – capital injection under subscription agreement dated [DD Month YYYY] – Beneficiary Account [NZ bank account number]'. Value is settled in NZD through the RBNZ-operated ESAS real-time gross settlement system, with same-day availability for large-value payments. On the compliance side, the inward remitting institution must obtain a funds-declaration certificate and the receiving bank will typically request a signed declaration that the investment does not require consent under the Overseas Investment Act 2005; since the commercial activity is an AI/LLM API platform with non-sensitive business assets of a value well below the NZ$400 million statutory screening threshold, the transaction is per se not notifiable. No inward wire tax clearance certificate is required under New Zealand law.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury disbursements for the AI platform fall into two broad clearing categories. First, routine service payments—cloud compute charges, GPU cluster rentals, licensing, legal and tax advisory fees—will be executed via corporate multi-bank SWIFT MT103 messages with ISO 20022 purpose code 'SERV' (Services) or 'LICF' (License Fee); NZD-denominated domestic disbursements clear through the Payments NZ bulk electronic clearing system (BECS) over Direct Credit, with high-value NZD interbank payments settled over ESAS via MT202. Second, for hardware procurement (data-centre equipment, GPU servers, or dedicated circuit connectivity), a documentary standby or commercial letter of credit (LC) may be deployed, issued by the NZ Tier 1 bank and advised through a correspondent bank; although international commercial LCs are uncommon for pure service-based AI API businesses, they are permissible as a contingent payment vehicle for supply-chain resilience, settled at sight or at tenor via standard UCP 600 rules. Every outward remittance must pass automated sanctions and PEP screening, and the treasury operating manual should include an ISO 20022 purpose-code matrix aligned to the SWIFT CBPR+ migration, ensuring that the bank never misclassifies cross-border AI service revenue as a capital transfer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign exchange contracts (FX Forwards) between NZD and USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CNY, and AUD, priced off the wholesale swap curve, allowing the platform to lock in the NZD/USD rate for forecasted token-based export revenues within the confines of the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) 2002 Master Agreement, or the shorter-form NZ Bankers' Association (NZBA) master agreement for corporate treasuries.
FX swaps (roll-over swaps) for the staggered conversion of monthly USDC-derived USD balances into operational NZD liquidity, enabled on a same-day T+2 basis by the NZ licensed bank's dealing desk.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps for any medium-term structured funding or capital-escrow balance that requires NPR-to-NZD asset-liability matching; a plain-vanilla USD/NZD cross-currency swap is permitted without specific RBNZ authorisation, provided the counterparty is a registered bank and collateral margining aligns with the New Zealand margin rules for non-cleared derivatives.

Over-the-counter foreign currency options (European-style puts/calls on NZD vs major currencies), permissible where the platform holds an actual or anticipated exposure from overseas procurement or from multi-currency licensing receipts, subject to FMA-licensed derivative issuance and the qualifying financial entity classification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Company Confirmation Statement) and Annual Government Renewal Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cook Islands Financial Services Supervisory Authority (FSSA) - Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: filing and payment are due within 30 calendar days after the anniversary of incorporation; payment is required on or before the anniversary date to avoid a late fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late filing penalty of USD 100 per commenced month or part thereof is assessed by the Registrar; where the Annual Return and fee remain outstanding for more than 11 months after the anniversary, the Registrar issues a formal notice and may administratively strike the company off the International Companies Register under the International Companies Act 1981-82.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Office and Registered Agent Renewal Instruction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Cook Islands Registered Agent (maintaining the registered office under the International Companies Act 1981-82)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually as of the incorporation anniversary, typically bundled with the Annual Return; resignation of the incumbent agent takes effect 21 calendar days after written notice to the Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If no replacement licensed registered agent is appointed within the resignation notice period, the Registrar must strike the company off the Register; the entity then loses its International Company status and its tax-exempt characterization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register Annual Confirmation and UBO Attestation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent acting on behalf of the FSSA Registrar under the International Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Amendment Act 2019
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due not later than the date of the Annual Return filing (incorporation anniversary); any share transfer or change in significant beneficial ownership must be notified within 14 calendar days of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain the Beneficial Ownership Register, or submission of false or incomplete UBO information, is a criminal offence punishable by a fine up to USD 10,000; repeated default also grounds the Registrar's discretion to strike the company off and dissolve it.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Tax Exemption Status Declaration / Economic Substance Statement (conditional only)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cook Islands Ministry of Finance and Public Expenditure Management (Taxation Authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 6 months after the end of the company's accounting period, only where the International Company is deemed tax-resident in the Cook Islands, applies for treaty benefits, or carries on any activity within the domestic Cook Islands economy
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Misrepresentation or non-declaration of resident status can void the International Company's tax-exempt classification, retroactively expose profits to domestic corporate income tax under the Taxation Act 2021, and trigger regulatory strike-off proceedings through the Registrar.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit applies to a standard tax-exempt Cook Islands International Company. A mandatory statutory audit is triggered exclusively where the entity is licensed as an international bank under the Banking Act 2003, carries on insurance or captive insurance business under the Insurance Act, or is specifically directed by the Financial Services Supervisory Authority. A non-licensed AI/LLM API token platform is therefore audit-exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutory accounting framework is imposed on an exempt International Company; where financial statements are voluntarily prepared, IFRS as issued by the IASB (with NZ IFRS as an accepted practical equivalent) is the prevailing standard. Any audit engagement that is nevertheless commissioned must be conducted in accordance with International Standards on Auditing (ISA).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register at its registered office. At each incorporation anniversary, coincident with the Annual Return filing, the company must confirm to its licensed registered agent the identity of all ultimate beneficial owners, disclose whether any shareholding transfer occurred during the preceding year, and update the register within 14 calendar days of any transfer or change. The registered agent validates the information against certified identification documentation and attests the confirmation to the Registrar.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (with nominee and beneficial ownership markers)
Minute Book and record of written resolutions
Register of Charges and Mortgages (if any)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 2,500 per annum for a licensed Cook Islands registered agent (standard registered office and compliance service; nominee officer services invoiced separately where engaged)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 12,000 per annum, applicable only where the International Company is an international bank, an insurer, or FSSA-directed; an ordinary AI/LLM API licensing company is audit-exempt

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand imposes a 28% corporate income tax rate on resident companies. Non-resident companies deriving New Zealand-source income are generally subject to final non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) or income tax on assessed income where no withholding tax applies. No general statutory tax holiday is available, but the 'look-through company' rules and certain R&D tax credits (15% on eligible R&D expenditure for the 2024/25 tax year under the RDTI regime) may reduce the effective tax rate for qualifying operations. The AI/LLM API platform structure, to the extent held by a foreign-owned non-resident company, should rely on thin capitalisation rules (maximum 60% debt-to-asset ratio for related-party debt) rather than any preferential effective rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed via myIR (Inland Revenue's secure online portal), with electronic filing required for all standard corporate taxpayers. Provisional tax payments are made via the Provisional Tax instalment system (3 instalments for standard balance dates unless GST ratio option or AIM is used).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR4 return and terminal tax payment are due by the 7th day of the fourth month after the company's balance date (e.g. for a 31 March balance date, 7 July). If an agent with a valid extension is used, the extended filing deadline is typically 31 March of the following year, or a later date prescribed by Inland Revenue for tax agents; terminal tax remains due at the original date unless an extension of time payment arrangement is granted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: New Zealand sourced income - total assessable income derived in New Zealand, excluding exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies (including foreign-owned ICs with a New Zealand fixed establishment or deriving NZ-source income) must declare only New Zealand-sourced assessable income. No foreign income is included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Overseas sourced income - foreign-sourced income taxable to a New Zealand resident company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Leave nil unless the entity is a New Zealand tax resident under the NZ incorporation/management rules. A pure non-resident IC with no New Zealand control or management should leave this box blank.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income before expenses (total assessable income less exempt income and adjustments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only gross New Zealand-source revenue from AI/LLM API services, licensing, or infrastructure utilisation attributable to the New Zealand permanent establishment or source rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total business expenses claimed against assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may deduct expenses to the extent they are incurred in deriving New Zealand-source assessable income, subject to apportionment rules. Transfer pricing documentation should justify any related-party cost allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (assessable income less allowable deductions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computed after applying New Zealand transfer pricing adjustments and thin capitalisation interest limitation rules.

Non-resident companies may carry forward losses only if the 49% continuity of ownership test is satisfied at all times during the income year. A foreign-owned IC with changing non-resident shareholders must closely monitor shareholder continuity.
Apply the 28% rate to net taxable income. Non-resident companies are not entitled to the smaller business tax rate (not applicable in New Zealand).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) deducted or deemed paid on assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For income subject to NRWT at source (royalties, interest, dividends), the NRWT is a final tax unless the income is attributable to a New Zealand PE, in which case the income is assessed on a net basis with a credit for NRWT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, R&D tax credits, and RWT credits on bank interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim treaty credits only if the relevant Double Tax Agreement applies and an IRD tax credit election is made. A certificate of residence (IR871 form or equivalent) should be uplifted before claiming treaty relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: an initial non-compliance penalty of NZ$250 for late IR4 filing, plus a further NZ$50 per month thereafter, capped at NZ$1,000 for any single return. Late payment penalties: 1% of the unpaid tax per day for the first day, then 1% per month thereafter (2% in the second month and 1% per month thereafter under the 'initial and incremental' late payment penalty regime). Use-of-money interest (UOMI) applies at the prescribed rate (currently approximately 8.73% per annum for underpayments as of 2024/25) on any underpaid provisional or terminal tax, regardless of whether the taxpayer holds a valid return-filing extension.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on fully imputed dividends is 0% for residents of treaty jurisdictions (including Australia, the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, Japan, Singapore, and China) where an approved resident withholding tax (RWT) rate of 0% applies to New Zealand resident shareholders. For all other non-resident shareholders, the NRWT rate on non-imputed or partially imputed dividends is 30%; on fully imputed dividends it is 15%, and the standard treaty rate is generally 15% (Australia 15%, United States 15%, China 15% for portfolio; 5% for significant holdings of at least 10% in the paying company, subject to limitation on benefits provisions).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke reduced withholding rates under a Double Tax Agreement, the non-resident recipient must, before payment or within the time frame allowed by Inland Revenue, complete and submit a 'Certificate of Residence' for New Zealand withholding tax purposes (Inland Revenue form IR871) to the New Zealand payer. The certificate must carry an official tax residence stamp or position of the foreign tax authority, and must be renewed if circumstances change. Without a valid certificate, the payer must deduct NRWT at the statutory 30% or 15% rate. The payer files a return of NRWT every quarter (Form IR67 or equivalent) and pays the tax by the 20th of the following month. As a practical matter, the beneficial owner of the AI/LLM API platform royalty or dividend income should hold a current tax residency certificate in its country of residence and provide it to the New Zealand withholding agent before each payment cycle.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on royalties and interest is 15% for non-residents, unless reduced by a Double Tax Agreement. Under the NZ-Australia DTA, royalty and interest rates are 10% (interest paid to a financial institution 0-10%); under the NZ-USA DTA, royalties and interest are 10%. For a China-incorporated IC, the NZ-China DTA provides a 10% rate on royalties and 10% on interest (with a 5% rate for interest paid to a bank or financial institution). The AI/LLM API platform's licensing of software, patent rights, or API access fees that effectively represent royalties for the use of IP will be subject to NRWT at the applicable treaty rate, unless the payment is for the supply of services (which is generally taxable only if attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment). All royalty payments to a non-resident must be reported to Inland Revenue on Form IR67 and the NRWT deducted at the time of payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Inland Revenue's transfer pricing rules (Part 4A of the Income Tax Act 2007) require cross-border related-party transactions to be conducted at arm's length. There is no statutory monetary threshold for preparing Local/Master File documentation, but Inland Revenue's operational statement and administrative guidelines require contemporaneous documentation for transactions exceeding NZ$3 million in aggregate annual related-party dealings, or NZ$1 million for any single category of related-party transaction involving AI/ML services or intangible-backed payments. A multinational group with total NZ turnover exceeding a prescribed threshold (commonly justified by reference to the OECD Action 13 framework, as adopted in Inland Revenue guidance) must keep a Master File and a Local File available on request. For the AI/LLM API platform, the material intercompany flows include SaaS-like fees, API usage fees, GPU cloud service charges, and software royalty payments; these must be documented using a contemporaneous OECD-aligned transfer pricing study, including a functional analysis and economic benchmarking.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate a separate Economic Substance Regulations regime in the manner of the UAE; however, New Zealand tax law and general anti-avoidance rules (Part 5A of the Tax Administration Act 1994 and the statutory General Anti-Avoidance Rule in section BG 1 and GB 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007) require that an entity claiming New Zealand tax benefits have real economic substance. A non-resident company in the structure must demonstrate actual business purpose, substantive decision-making, staff, assets, and risks adequate to its functions. The use of a Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) in this jurisdiction analysis implies a regional structure where the IC is tax resident in the Cook Islands under its own tax law, not in New Zealand; however, if central management and control is exercised from New Zealand, the IRD may assert New Zealand tax residence and apply the full corporate tax regime. Under the New Zealand general anti-avoidance rules, a series of transactions designed to shift profits out of New Zealand without changing the economic position of the group is void against the Commissioner, potentially triggering reconstructing adjustments and penalties up to 100% of the shortfall, plus interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax Avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting New Zealand-source AI/LLM API revenue derived via a New Zealand fixed establishment or client-facing activity, or shifting profits to the non-resident parent through artificial invoicing, backdated licences or a sham contract without any real services or substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Shortfall penalties under section 141E of the Tax Administration Act 1994: 50% of the tax shortfall for abusive tax avoidance, increasing to 100% if the dominant purpose is tax evasion or fraud. In addition, late payment penalties, use-of-money interest from the original due date, and criminal prosecution under section 143 or 144 may result in fines up to NZ$150,000 (25 times the tax shortfall for evasion) and imprisonment terms up to 5 years in the case of wilful evasion or aiding and abetting tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a New Zealand-registered or New Zealand-managed IC may be personally liable in equity for any tax unpaid by the company if the company's business has been carried on recklessly or fraudulently (section 135 and 136 of the Companies Act 1993, and section 115 of the Tax Administration Act 1994). The Commissioner can issue a director penalty notice (section 166) requiring payment of unpaid PAYE, GST, RWT, NRWT or other withholding taxes. Directors may face an order for civil recovery, a travel ban under the High Court's inherent jurisdiction where assets are dissipated, and personal disqualification. Criminal prosecution may also be brought against 'persons concerned with the management' of the company, including a shadow director or offshore shareholder director who participates in the decision to defraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) as a pure nominee-owned shell that has no staff, no office, no bank account with actual transaction monitoring, no independent board decisions, and whose entire business is the licensing of APIs or the receipt of royalties while central management and control is actually exercised from New Zealand,
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The IRD may under the general anti-avoidance rule apply the reconstruction rules in section GA 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007 to treat the arrangement as void against the Commissioner, with the tax consequences determined as if the avoidance scheme had not occurred. This may lead to a 50% abusive tax position shortfall penalty, a 100% evasion penalty if intentional, and the disallowance of all expenditure attributable to the sham. In addition, the '100% entity' is treated as New Zealand resident under the dual-residence tie-breaks in an applicable DTA; the company can be assessed on its worldwide income, and any intercompany royalties paid offshore are disallowed as a deduction if the underlying IP ownership does not reflect the economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the shell company, including offshore nominee directors who act without questioning the commercial reality, may be found to have breached their fiduciary duties under the Companies Act 1993. They may be jointly and severally liable to pay the company's unpaid tax (section 115 TAA), be prohibited from managing a company for up to 5 years under section 382 of the Companies Act 1993, and be subject to asset freezing orders and travel bans while an investigation is pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Thin Capitalisation Misstatement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for a NZ$3 million+ annual related-party AI/LLM API licence, or mispricing the API usage and SaaS revenue such that the New Zealand PE earns no more than a token 2-3% margin while the offshore IC retains 90% of the economic profit, with no defensible functional risk analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner may make a transfer pricing adjustment under Part 4A of the Income Tax Act 2007 and section GC 12, recalculating the taxable income at arm's length. The resulting tax shortfall is subject to a 20% shortfall penalty for taking an unacceptable tax position, or 50% for an abusive tax position with dominant tax avoidance purpose. Late payment penalties and UOMI apply. The thin capitalisation rules (section FE 4) disallow interest deductions to the extent that the New Zealand group's related-party debt exceeds 60% of its net assets, and the financial arrangement rules may deny deductions on hybrid mismatches involving convertible notes or excessive non-resident related-party debt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve a tax return with an incorrect transfer pricing position may be jointly and severally liable for the resulting shortfall to the extent they caused or permitted the misstatement. Under section 141EB TAA, a taxpayer is liable for a 100% penalty for suppressing a document, or for knowingly providing false information to the tax agent. Directors may also be charged with an offence under section 143A for evading the collection or payment of tax, carrying penalties up to NZ$150,000 for an individual and imprisonment for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CTF and Financial Crime Violation in Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Stripe/USDC payment rails while failing to conduct adequate anti-money laundering and countering financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) customer due diligence for API customers; allowing the platform to be used to launder cryptocurrency proceeds; or failing to declare cryptocurrency proceeds for tax purposes, particularly where USDC payments are received into an offshore wallet without proper recordkeeping.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 applies to financial institutions, including those dealing in virtual assets. A reporting entity that fails to conduct CDD, develop a compliance programme, or report suspicious transactions faces civil penalties of up to NZ$200,000 for each contravention and NZ$10 million for repeated serious contraventions. Individuals who knowingly launder the proceeds of criminal activity are liable under the Crimes Act 1961 (sections 243-245) to imprisonment up to 7 years. Failure to report a suspicious transaction attracts penalties; in the tax context, undeclared USDC-to-fiat conversions are taxable as income or capital gains depending on the holding, and omission may trigger the evasion penalties and criminal liability described above.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers may be prosecuted under the AML/CFT Act where the failure results from their personal conduct or neglect; penalties include imprisonment of up to 12 months for a knowingly false statement to the FIU, and unlimited compensation orders. Directors of an IC who personally move USDC into a New Zealand bank account, or who control the API payment wallet, may be personally liable for AML penalty fines if the business operates without an adequate compliance programme. Travel bans can be imposed under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009, and directors' offshore assets may be restrained.
